papers.title: From Adiposity to Diastolic Dysfunction: The Integrated Role of Epicardial Fat, Autonomic Dysregulation, and Morning Blood Pressure Surge in Obesity.
papers.abstract: Although the association between obesity and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) is well established, the concurrent associations of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), sleep-trough (prewaking) morning blood pressure surge (MBPS), and autonomic imbalance with LVDD have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EAT thickness, MBPS, and heart rate variability (HRV) parameters with LVDD in obese adults and to assess the cross-sectional discriminatory performance of these multimodal markers. This cross-sectional study included 240 individuals, comprising 120 obese participants (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2) and 120 age- and sex-matched normal-weight controls (body mass index 18.5-24.9 kg/m2). All participants underwent transthoracic echocardiography, 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, and 24-h Holter electrocardiographic analysis, with HRV data available for the entire cohort (n = 240). EAT thickness was measured echocardiographically, and LVDD was classified using contemporary guideline-based echocardiographic criteria. SDNN was predefined as the primary autonomic marker, while RMSSD and the LF/HF ratio were reported as supportive indices. Associations with LVDD (≥ Grade I) were evaluated using correlation analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Cross-sectional discrimination analysis and performance assessment were performed within the obese subgroup (n = 120). Compared with controls, obese participants exhibited greater EAT thickness (6.5 ± 1.7 vs. 4.0 ± 1.2 mm), higher MBPS (33 ± 10 vs. 21 ± 7 mmHg), increased LF/HF ratio, and lower SDNN and RMSSD values (all p < 0.001). The prevalence of LVDD was significantly higher in obese individuals than in controls (45% vs. 15%, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, EAT thickness (odds ratio [OR] = 1.20 per 1 mm; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08-1.34), MBPS (OR = 1.35 per 10 mmHg; 95% CI 1.10-1.65), and SDNN (OR = 0.88 per 10 ms; 95% CI 0.80-0.97) were independently associated with LVDD. The parsimonious model demonstrated discrimination and calibration comparable to or superior to the full clinical model (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.85). In obese adults, increased epicardial adiposity, exaggerated MBPS, and autonomic dysfunction coexist with LVDD. Integrated assessment of structural (EAT), hemodynamic (MBPS), and autonomic (SDNN) markers may facilitate cross-sectional identification of LVDD and improve phenotypic characterization in obesity.

papers.title: Effect of Tai Chi Exercise on Fatigue in Renal Transplant Recipients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a prevalent symptom in kidney transplant patients that not only affects quality of life but may also impact long-term graft survival. While Tai Chi has been shown to effectively reduce fatigue in patients with chronic diseases, research in kidney transplant recipients remains limited. To explore the effects of Tai Chi exercise on fatigue among kidney transplant recipients and to investigate the effectiveness and safety of Tai Chi-based rehabilitation. A prospective, single-center, parallel-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in Northeast China. The study period for patient recruitment and intervention implementation was from 1 June 2025, to 12 October 2025. Eligible participants were kidney transplant recipients aged 18-60 years who were at least 1 month post-transplantation. Sixty-four kidney transplant patients were randomly allocated (1:1) to the intervention group (Tai Chi exercise) or the control group (routine care only). The intervention group received a 12-week Tai Chi exercise program. The primary outcome was fatigue severity assessed at 12 weeks. After 12 weeks of Tai Chi intervention, there were statistically significant differences in total fatigue scores between the two groups of renal transplant recipients. Sleep quality and 6-min walk distance were significantly improved. Tai Chi exercise is a gentle and well-tolerated exercise intervention that can effectively improve fatigue in renal transplant recipients. Trial Registration: International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry: 2026000360.

papers.title: Which Domains of Cognition in Older Adults Are Affected by Sleep Duration? A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, research on the impact of sleep duration on cognitive domains in older adults has been emerging; however, a formal synthesis of the focused literature that addresses all cognitive domains has not yet been conducted. Therefore, this review study was conducted to investigate the effects of sleep duration on various cognitive domains in older adults. This scoping review was conducted according to Arksey and O'Malley (2005). A systematic search was conducted across three research databases: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus, with relevant gray literature also reviewed. Studies that reported on the relationship between sleep duration and cognition among older adults were included in the review. Data were extracted, charted, and synthesized into a narrative. Consistent with the purpose of a scoping review, the methodological quality of the studies was not appraised. A total of 23 studies published between 2009 and 2024 fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The findings revealed that both excessively long and short sleep durations were strongly linked to impairments in learning, memory, and complex attention. Only a limited number of studies explored all cognitive domains, with none addressing social cognition. Additionally, analyses considering gender differences were notably absent. This review highlights cognitive domains affected by inadequate sleep in older adults and emphasizes the need for more research on gender-specific differences in sleep duration. It also pointed out a gap in understanding the link between sleep duration and social cognition, emphasizing the need for further studies in this area.

papers.title: Circadian mechanisms in heart failure: Cell-specific regulation and chrono-medicine.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that circadian rhythms profoundly influence the pathophysiology of heart failure (HF). The circadian clock system governs myocardial functions via synchronized actions from multiple cell types involving cardiomyocytes and non-cardiomyocytes. This review summarizes state-of-the-art advances on the cardiovascular circadian system and provides a perspective on time-of-day effects in the pathophysiology of HF, including energy metabolism, tissue inflammation and fibrosis. In particular, we focus on cell-specific circadian regulation and synthesize how circadian clocks across cardiomyocytes, vascular cells, fibroblasts, and adipocytes interact to regulate the pathophysiology of HF. Based on this framework, we discuss how synchronizing internal and external time cues via clock-modulating compounds and/or time-restricted eating (TRE) may prevent HF or facilitate rehabilitation. Together, this Review provides a timely synthesis of current understanding of HF as a function of biological timing and highlights potential chronotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.abstract: Acute cognitive challenge produces consistent changes in several EEG indices, including alpha-band desynchronization, frontocentral theta enhancement, beta-band activity, and the theta/beta ratio. These measures serve as common biomarkers of cognitive workload and stress. It is not yet clear whether chronic occupational exposure to high cognitive demand alters these responses. Emergency physicians offer a useful test case, since their work involves repeated cognitive control under time pressure and high-stakes decision-making. We recorded 19-channel electroencephalography from 17 board-certified emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during eyes-open rest and a standardized composite challenge combining Stroop interference, serial subtraction, time pressure, and evaluative feedback. Spectral power was estimated with Welch's method, log-transformed, and analyzed using a hierarchical framework combining six a priori regional features with electrode-wise topographic mapping. Across groups, the challenge produced robust frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta, consistent with workload-related cortical engagement. No Group x Condition interaction survived false discovery rate correction for the regional features, and no exploratory electrode-wise interaction survived correction across the full feature set. A complementary Bayesian analysis yielded moderate evidence for the null for the alpha and theta features, but inconclusive evidence for the beta and theta/beta features. Sub-band decomposition showed the challenge-related beta increase was specific to high beta (20-30 Hz), while low and mid beta decreased in emergency physicians. These results indicate an absence of detectable large group differences in EEG stress biomarkers following prolonged occupational exposure to high cognitive demand, although the sample constrains this conclusion to large effects.

papers.title: Controlled deep breathing technique intervention effects on resting EEG, subjective psychological distress, and executive function performance in young adults.
papers.abstract: Controlled breathing techniques have been widely investigated for their role in emotional regulation; however, their effects on resting-state neural oscillatory activity and psychological distress remain insufficiently characterized. The present study examined whether a Controlled Deep Breathing Technique (CDBT) intervention modulates resting-state electroencephalographic (EEG) activity and subjective psychological distress in healthy adults. Forty healthy adults (ages 18 to 40 years) were randomly assigned to an experimental (CDBT) or control (natural breathing) intervention group for 20 min. Resting-state quantitative EEG (qEEG) was recorded before and after the intervention under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Behavioral measures included assessments of subjective psychological distress and executive functioning. qEEG analyses during resting-state focused on alpha/beta power ratios at frontal and parietal electrodes. Results showed a significant increase in alpha/beta ratios in the experimental group compared with the control group, particularly during the eyes-closed condition and at parietal electrodes. The experimental group also showed significant reductions in psychological distress scores and improvements in executive functioning measures, whereas no significant changes were observed in the control group. These findings suggest that CDBT may modulate frontoparietal oscillatory dynamics associated with relaxed mental states and improved executive functioning, providing preliminary evidence that CDBT may influence emotional regulation and cognitive control in healthy adults.

papers.title: A pilot study of invasive vagus nerve stimulation in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease: preliminary results on safety, cognition, and biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with no curative therapies, and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory approach. This prospective, open-label pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary cognitive, psychological, inflammatory, and AD biomarker effects of invasive VNS (iVNS) in Chinese AD patients. Five AD patients (mean age: 62.4 ± 4.0 years) underwent iVNS implantation, with assessments at baseline, 3, and 6 months postoperatively (one patient did not complete the 6-month follow-up). Cognitive function (MMSE, CDR, VFT, BNT), psychological/behavioral symptoms (CMAI, HAMA, HAMD), sleep/daily-living status (ESS, ADL), serum inflammatory factors, and AD biomarkers were measured. Among cognitive outcomes, MMSE increased by 1 point at both follow-ups and VFT rose by 5.2 and 4.25 points at 3 and 6 months, respectively, although none of these changes reached statistical significance; global CDR remained unchanged. HAMA and HAMD scores decreased, and ESS scores declined by 25-27%, without reaching significance. Serum pro-inflammatory Eotaxin and CCL5 were significantly reduced (p = 0.026 and p = 0.045, respectively), whereas CXCL10 levels showed a non-significant numerical increase. Although the Aβ42 and Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio showed numerical increases (by 126.4% and 75.3%) and pTau181, pTau217, and NfL showed numerical decreases, these changes were not statistically significant. Only transient hoarseness was reported. These preliminary findings suggest that iVNS is feasible and associated with early signals of cognitive, psychological, inflammatory, and biomarker changes in AD patients, which warrant confirmation in larger, randomized, sham-controlled trials.

papers.title: Neurobiological mechanisms and brain network dysfunction in major depressive disorder: an integrative review.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent and disabling psychiatric disorder characterized by persistent mood disturbances, cognitive impairments, and significant systemic consequences. Despite its substantial clinical burden, diagnosis remains challenging because current approaches rely largely on subjective symptom-based assessments and are complicated by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity. In this review, we synthesize findings from neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and molecular studies to provide an integrated overview of the structural, functional, and neurobiological alterations that underlie MDD. We discuss abnormalities involving large-scale brain networks, neuroplasticity and stress-related pathways, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neurotransmitter systems, together with their implications for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response. Collectively, current evidence implicates both molecular dysregulation and large-scale neural network dysfunction in MDD, although direct evidence linking alterations across these biological levels remains limited. Integrating multimodal biological and neuroimaging approaches may improve diagnostic precision, facilitate personalized therapeutic strategies, and advance the development of biologically informed psychiatry.

papers.title: Vortioxetine-Associated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep Alterations: A Focused Narrative Review of Human Polysomnographic Evidence.
papers.abstract: This focused narrative review examines the relationship between vortioxetine and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and considers the potential clinical significance of REM-related changes observed during treatment. Direct human polysomnographic evidence remains very limited and is derived principally from two studies. The review integrates relevant sleep neurobiology, vortioxetine pharmacology, and human polysomnographic findings while distinguishing biological plausibility from demonstrated clinical significance. The available evidence is interpreted cautiously because changes in individual REM measures do not necessarily represent a uniform alteration of REM physiology and an objective polysomnographic effect should not be assumed to reflect a therapeutic mechanism. At present, vortioxetine-associated REM changes are best regarded as a pharmacodynamic effect whose persistence, dose dependence, underlying mechanism, and clinical relevance remain uncertain. These changes have not been established as surrogate markers of antidepressant response or other meaningful patient outcomes. Further prospective research integrating objective sleep measures with symptoms, subjective sleep quality, daytime functioning, cognition, and longer-term outcomes is needed to clarify the significance of vortioxetine-associated REM alterations.

papers.title: Beyond physical isolation: behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological mechanisms of functional social isolation.
papers.abstract: Functional Social Isolation (FSI) describes a proposed form of social disconnection in the digital era, wherein individuals are physically co-present yet psychologically detached during pervasive digital immersion. This review examines how everyday digital immersion may contribute to persistent social disengagement, outlines its behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological pathways, and discusses its implications for public health and behavioral psychology. By synthesizing emerging literature on co-present digital immersion, social buffering, and neuroendocrine regulation, we identify five behavioral correlates relevant to FSI: attentional fragmentation, habitual or problematic online engagement, emotional volatility, avoidance of offline social interaction, and reduced practice of offline social skills. We also consider evidence concerning oxytocin, dopamine, norepinephrine, endocannabinoids, serotonin, and cortisol, alongside models of internet-related behaviors. These systems may represent candidate pathways linking digital immersion, attentional capture, affective regulation, and reduced engagement with available social partners. However, current neurobiological evidence is largely indirect and is not specific to FSI; similar patterns may arise from traditional social isolation, chronic stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, or depression. We therefore present a hypothetical multi-system framework intended to generate testable predictions rather than establish an FSI-specific neurochemical state. FSI may be modifiable through interventions that reduce digital interruptions during face-to-face interaction and support meaningful synchronous engagement. Future research should validate its measurement, test causal pathways, and evaluate interventions across populations and social contexts.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals are of great significance in human-computer interaction and affective computing, as they can objectively reflect transient neural dynamics in the brain. However, existing methods still face several challenges, including limited training samples, susceptibility of EEG signals to noise interference, and insufficient granularity in conventional two-dimensional emotion models. To address these issues, this study proposes VAD-EmotionNet, an EEG-based emotion recognition model built upon the three-dimensional valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) emotional space. Specifically, the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) is employed to extract non-stationary differential entropy (DE) features for constructing volumetric spatial-spectral representations. Moreover, a multi-query spatial-spectral attention (MQSSA) network is introduced to constrain head-specific representational flexibility through shared key-value projections while modeling long-range spatial dependencies across EEG channels. In addition, a cosine temporal inference correction (CTIC) module is designed to optimize feature distributions on a hypersphere using supervised contrastive loss, thereby smoothing local prediction anomalies. The proposed model is evaluated on the DEAP and DREAMER benchmark datasets using leave-one-trial-out (LOTO) cross-validation. Experimental results demonstrate that VAD-EmotionNet achieves competitive performance across multiple classification tasks, highlighting its strong capability in decoding complex neural representations. These findings lay a solid foundation for the real-world application of emotion-aware systems within a 3D affective space.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance and its associations with night shift work, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among urban operation-supporting workers: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is common among occupational populations and may vary by work schedules and psychological burdens. However, evidence among urban operation-supporting occupational groups remains limited. This study aimed to compare the prevalence of sleep disturbance among healthcare, environmental sanitation, and transportation workers in Chongqing, China, and to examine the associations of night shift work, anxiety, and depressive symptoms with sleep disturbance. This study was based on the Health Literacy Surveillance Project for Key Occupational Groups in Chongqing (June-September 2022). Overall, 3,667 front-line workers were included. Sleep disturbance was assessed using the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention sleep quality scale. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, respectively. Modified Poisson regression models with robust variance estimation were used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Interaction terms were further included to examine occupational group differences. The prevalence of sleep disturbance was 94.1, 85.1, and 92.8% among healthcare, environmental sanitation, and transportation workers, respectively. After adjustment, environmental sanitation workers had a lower prevalence of sleep disturbance than healthcare workers (aPR = 0.904, 95% CI: 0.862-0.947, p < 0.001), whereas transportation workers showed no significant difference (aPR = 0.996, 95% CI: 0.956-1.037, p = 0.839). Night shift work (aPR = 1.025, 95% CI: 1.003-1.048, p = 0.028) and anxiety symptoms (aPR = 1.094, 95% CI: 1.073-1.116, p < 0.001) were associated with a higher prevalence of sleep disturbance. Depressive symptoms showed no statistical significance in the fully adjusted main model (aPR = 1.018, 95% CI: 0.999-1.038, p = 0.068). The environmental sanitation sector significantly interacted with anxiety symptoms (aPR = 1.082, 95% CI: 1.030-1.136, p = 0.002), suggesting a stronger anxiety-sleep disturbance association. No significant interactions were observed between occupational group and depressive symptoms or night shift work. Sleep disturbance was prevalent among urban operation-supporting occupational groups. Night shift work and anxiety symptoms were associated with sleep disturbance, with anxiety showing the most stable association. Depressive symptoms showed a weaker, model-dependent association. Sleep and mental health interventions may need to consider occupational context.

papers.title: Acute Kidney Injury Following Whole Cherry Consumption as a Sleep Aid in a Geriatric Patient With Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Cherries are consumed for their anti-inflammatory and sleep-promoting effects, but their potential adverse effects remain poorly characterized. A 95-year-old woman with stage 3A chronic kidney disease (CKD) presented with an increase in serum creatinine from a baseline of 0.8 to 1.3 mg/dL and a decrease in estimated glomerular filtration rate from 55.3 to 35.2 mL/min/1.73 m² following two weeks of consuming 15-20 fresh or frozen whole cherries nightly. Cherry consumption was discontinued, and her kidney function returned to baseline one month later. Cherries contain high amounts of anthocyanins, which may contribute to acute kidney injury (AKI) in CKD patients through cyclooxygenase (COX)-inhibitory mechanisms, similar to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Application of the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale yielded a score of 7, indicating a "probable" association between cherry consumption and AKI.

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated central nervous system (CNS) involvement in children is uncommon and may present with nonspecific neurological symptoms. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may remain normal, making diagnosis challenging. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) has emerged as a useful diagnostic tool, although positive EBV results require careful clinical interpretation. A previously healthy 5-year-old boy presented with fever (38.5 ℃), headache, dizziness, and nausea for 3 days without seizures, altered consciousness, focal neurological deficits, or ataxia. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. Brain MRI was unremarkable. CSF examination revealed an opening pressure of 120 mmH2O and mild pleocytosis (13×106/L, 100% mononuclear cells), with normal glucose and protein levels. CSF tNGS detected EBV (24,002 sequence reads; estimated pathogen concentration <103 copies/mL), while no other pathogens were identified and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies were negative. Serum EBV DNA was positive, and EBV serology demonstrated viral capsid antigen (VCA)-IgM positivity during the acute phase followed by VCA-IgG seroconversion during recovery. Electroencephalography (EEG) showed sharp and sharp-slow wave discharges in the left parietal, occipital, and posterior temporal regions despite normal MRI. The patient received intravenous ganciclovir (10 mg/kg twice daily for 2 weeks) and empirical ceftriaxone for 4 days. Clinical symptoms resolved completely, follow-up EEG normalized, and no neurological sequelae were observed at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights that possible EBV-associated CNS involvement may occur in children despite normal brain MRI and only mild CSF abnormalities. The combination of CSF tNGS, dynamic EBV serology, EEG findings, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and clinical follow-up may facilitate diagnosis. Because EBV detected in CSF does not necessarily indicate causation, results should always be interpreted in the context of the overall clinical presentation.

papers.title: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
papers.abstract: Windowed electroencephalography (EEG) pipelines can produce misleadingly high performance when segments from the same participant occur in both training and testing. We define this contamination as window leakage and test it in two clinically and technically distinct public cohorts: 121 children (61 attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder [ADHD], 60 controls) and 149 adults (100 Parkinson's disease, 49 controls). Signals were harmonized to 18 common channels and 128 Hz. All primary models used stratified 8-fold participant-disjoint evaluation, 50%-overlapping windows, participant-level probability aggregation, and validation participants drawn exclusively from each outer-training fold. A deliberately contaminated Random Forest audit contrasted random-window and participant-disjoint splitting. Random-window balanced accuracy reached 95.59% in ADHD and 92.02% in Parkinson's, but fell to 60.98% and 56.17%, respectively, when participants were held out. Thus, the inflation replicated across disorders, ages, recording tasks, and acquisition systems. Under correct evaluation, CNN-LSTM achieved the highest ADHD subject-level balanced accuracy (73.21%), whereas EEGNet achieved the highest Parkinson's balanced accuracy (63.75%). No architecture comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction. One-, 2-, 4-, and 8-s windows produced no consistent cross-cohort ranking. Removing ATCNN-SA components also yielded dataset-dependent changes, and no ablation difference was significant after correction. Participant-bootstrap intervals remained wide despite tens of thousands of windows, indicating that inferential precision was governed by participant count rather than segment count. Window-level random splits contaminate clinical EEG performance estimates and must not be used to claim generalization to unseen individuals. Participants should be separated before model fitting, results should be reported at subject level, and split, windowing, aggregation, and uncertainty procedures should be disclosed explicitly.

papers.title: Correlation of peripheral blood BMAL1 level with non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease patients.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to quantify BMAL1 expression in the peripheral blood of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and to evaluate its correlation with non-motor symptoms (NMS). We further assessed whether serum interleukin-6 and melatonin levels were associated with BMAL1 expression. This study included 80 patients with PD and 80 age-and sex-matched healthy controls. General clinical information and scores on multiple NMS scales were collected. Peripheral blood BMAL1 expression was quantified using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Serum levels of melatonin and interleukin-6 were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Spearman's correlation analysis was used to evaluate the associations between BMAL1 expression and the NMS scores. Compared to healthy controls, patients with PD exhibited significantly lower peripheral blood BMAL1 expression levels in the morning (p = 0.005). BMAL1 levels were negatively correlated with the NMS Scale score (r = -0.407, p < 0.001). Furthermore, higher BMAL1 levels were associated with better night-time sleep quality and cognitive function, whereas lower BMAL1 levels correlated with more severe anxiety and depression. A weak positive correlation was observed between BMAL1 expression and melatonin levels (r = 0.267, p = 0.017). A significant negative correlation was found between BMAL1 expression and interleukin-6 level (r = -0.603, p < 0.001). In this cross-sectional study, peripheral blood BMAL1 expression at a single morning time point was lower in patients with PD and correlated with NMS severity, suggesting a potential pathway involving BMAL1, melatonin, and inflammatory cytokines in NMS pathogenesis. Future studies with multiple time-point measurements are required to validate these findings.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review of Clinical Features, Impact and Interventions.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by social-communication deficits, restricted-repetitive behaviors, and sensory anomalies. Sleep disturbances are reported to significantly worsen behavioral, cognitive, and family functioning in ASD. This scoping review aims to map existing evidence on the clinical features, impact, and interventions for sleep disturbances in children with ASD. A comprehensive literature review was conducted in accordance with PRISM-ScR guidelines, and searches were performed in PubMed, Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), Cochrane, Scopus, and Embase. Studies published from 2015 to August 31, 2025, were identified using combinations of the terms "Sleep disturbances," "ASD," "Prevalence," "Etiology," "Types," and "Intervention." Eligible studies included systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and case series published in peer-reviewed English-language journals involving children and adolescents with ASD. The reviewed literature indicates multifactorial causes for sleep disturbances in ASD, including medical/psychiatric comorbidities and behavioral factors like sensory sensitivities and bedtime resistance. Common sleep problems include insomnia, circadian rhythm disorders, parasomnias, sleep-disordered breathing, and sleep-related movement disorders (SRMDs). These disturbances exacerbate core ASD symptoms, impair adaptive functioning, contribute to aggression, and increase parental stress. Reported interventions include caregiver education, behavioral strategies, pharmacological approaches, and management of comorbid sleep-related conditions. Sleep disturbances in children with ASD are highly prevalent, multifaceted, and clinically significant. Early identification and evidence-based, integrative interventions may improve sleep quality, behavioral outcomes, and overall family well-being. Future research should focus on longitudinal designs and objective sleep assessment methods to strengthen the evidence base.

papers.title: Respiratory event duration reveals novel phenotypes beyond the apnea-hypopnea index in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep. Although the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the cornerstone of OSA diagnosis and severity assessment, it primarily reflects the frequency of respiratory events and may not adequately capture differences in respiratory event duration or the associated physiological burden. We aimed to identify novel OSA phenotypes by incorporating respiratory event duration into polysomnography-based cluster analysis. We retrospectively analyzed consecutive adult patients with OSA who underwent overnight polysomnography. Demographic, anthropometric, and polysomnographic characteristics were collected. Age, body mass index (BMI), neck circumference, AHI, lowest oxygen saturation (LowSpO₂), longest apnea duration (LAP), and longest hypopnea duration (LHP) were included in the clustering analysis. Hierarchical clustering using Ward's method was first performed to determine the optimal number of clusters, followed by K-means clustering to identify distinct OSA phenotypes. Among 999 consecutive patients, 959 with complete clustering variables were included in the final analysis. Hierarchical clustering followed by K-means clustering identified four distinct OSA phenotypes. Cluster 1 represented a mild phenotype characterized by the lowest AHI, the shortest LAP, and preserved nocturnal oxygenation. Cluster 2 represented an obesity-associated severe phenotype with the highest BMI, the largest neck circumference, the highest AHI, and the greatest degree of nocturnal oxygen desaturation. Cluster 3 was characterized by markedly prolonged apnea duration despite only moderate AHI, whereas Cluster 4 exhibited the longest apnea and hypopnea durations accompanied by pronounced nocturnal hypoxemia. Significant differences were observed among the four phenotypes in demographic characteristics, obesity-related measures, disease severity, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory event duration (all P < 0.001). Importantly, respiratory event duration provided additional temporal characterization across phenotypes beyond conventional frequency-based severity assessment. Respiratory event duration-enhanced clustering identified four exploratory OSA phenotypes with distinct temporal characteristics. These findings suggest that respiratory event duration may provide complementary information to conventional AHI-based severity assessment, while its clinical utility requires further validation.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging and electrophysiological signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment with different amyloid-β deposition status: correlations with cognitive function and diagnostic value.
papers.abstract: Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) is a heterogeneous transitional cognitive state between normal aging and dementia. Aβ positivity elevates dementia conversion risk but does not equate to prodromal Alzheimer's disease (AD), and not all Aβ-positive aMCI individuals progress to clinical AD dementia. Distinguishing Aβ-positive from Aβ-negative aMCI facilitates pathological subtyping rather than definitive early AD diagnosis. This cross-sectional study aimed to characterize scalp-level resting-state EEG and structural MRI signatures specific to Aβ-positive aMCI, explore their covariate-adjusted correlations with cognitive performance and regional Aβ burden, and develop an internally validated multimodal auxiliary classification model for Aβ stratification. Fifty enrolled aMCI participants (30 Aβ-positive, 20 Aβ-negative) and 35 cognitively normal controls (NC) completed unified 20-min eyes-closed resting-state scalp EEG, 3.0 T structural MRI, 18F-AV45 amyloid PET and 18F-FDG cerebral metabolism PET examinations. Artifact-free scalp EEG spectral power and regional θ/α ratio were calculated via Welch spectral analysis; voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was adopted to quantify whole-brain gray matter volume. Covariate-controlled partial correlation corrected for multiple comparisons was applied to evaluate cross-modal associations among cortical Aβ SUVR load, cerebral glucose metabolism and domain-specific cognitive scores. A binary logistic regression classification model combining screened EEG and MRI markers was established, with DeLong test for ROC curve comparison and 1,000-bootstrap internal validation. (1) Relative to Aβ-negative aMCI and NC groups, the Aβ-positive subgroup presented significantly elevated whole-scalp θ relative power and scalp θ/α ratio, decreased scalp α and β relative power (all q < 0.05, FDR-corrected), with predominant scalp oscillatory alterations distributed over temporal, parietal and occipital scalp electrode clusters. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio yielded optimal classification performance for Aβ stratification (AUC = 0.875). (2) The Aβ-positive subgroup showed significant gray matter atrophy across 13 AD-vulnerable brain regions including bilateral fusiform gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, parahippocampal gyrus, precuneus and right entorhinal cortex (all q < 0.05), with the maximum effect size identified in the right precuneus (partial η 2 = 0.477, AUC = 0.778). (3) Within the Aβ-positive subgroup, the temporal scalp θ/α ratio was positively correlated with medial temporal Aβ SUVR (r = 0.501, 95% CI [0.146, 0.732], q = 0.030); right precuneus gray matter volume was negatively correlated with multi-region cortical Aβ burden (q < 0.05). Left parahippocampal gyrus volume was positively correlated with MoCA memory subscores (r = 0.479, 95% CI [0.118, 0.709], q < 0.05). No significant associations between scalp EEG metrics and FDG glucose metabolism survived FDR correction. (4) The multimodal logistic regression model integrating temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume achieved favorable classification efficacy for Aβ-positive aMCI differentiation (AUC = 0.852, 95% CI [0.748, 0.955]), with good calibration and clinical net benefit based solely on internal bootstrap validation. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume are promising candidate non-invasive auxiliary biomarkers for Aβ pathological stratification in aMCI, rather than validated clinical diagnostic biomarkers. The multimodal model provides supplementary subtyping value within this single-center cohort, while external multicenter validation is mandatory before clinical application. This cross-sectional dataset cannot support prediction of longitudinal progression to AD dementia.

papers.title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. UMIN000053211.

papers.title: Dynamic EEG network responses to acupuncture stimulation in patients with stroke: a neurophysiological study.
papers.abstract: Acupuncture may modulate brain activity through effects on the central nervous system. This study aimed to investigate short-term changes in spontaneous EEG activity and functional connectivity during acupuncture in patients with stroke using multichannel electroencephalography (EEG). Multichannel EEG recordings were collected at three stages: before acupuncture, during acupuncture, and after acupuncture. Acupuncture was applied at Jianyu, Quchi, and Waiguan. EEG activity was evaluated using power spectral density (PSD) analysis. Functional connectivity was assessed using the weighted phase lag index (wPLI). Functional brain networks were constructed for different frequency bands. Graph theory analysis was used to examine clustering coefficient and global efficiency across different network sparsities. Power spectral density analysis showed significant stage-related changes in delta, theta, and alpha relative power, but not in beta power. Delta relative power decreased during acupuncture and partially recovered after acupuncture, but remained comparable to the pre-acupuncture level. Theta relative power increased during acupuncture and then decreased after acupuncture, with the post-acupuncture level lower than the pre-acupuncture level. Alpha relative power increased during acupuncture and decreased after acupuncture, but remained higher than the pre-acupuncture level. Whole-brain average wPLI showed a decrease in the delta band and an increase in the alpha band during acupuncture. No significant stage-related changes were observed in the theta-band average wPLI after correction for multiple comparisons. Graph-theoretical measures, including clustering coefficient and global efficiency, did not show statistically significant stage-related changes at the selected sparsity. Acupuncture was associated with short-term, frequency-dependent changes in spontaneous EEG activity and functional connectivity in patients with stroke. The observed changes were mainly reflected in spectral power and whole-brain average wPLI, while changes in overall network topology were not statistically supported. These findings provide preliminary neurophysiological evidence for the brain response to acupuncture stimulation.

papers.title: Smartphone addiction, physical activity engagement, and sleep quality in Chinese adolescents: a parallel and serial mediation model.
papers.abstract: Excessive smartphone use has become a major public health concern among adolescents, particularly in China where smartphone use is widespread. Although smartphone addiction is consistently associated with poor sleep quality, the mechanisms underlying this association remain insufficiently understood. This study examined whether physical activity engagement and depressive symptoms operate as parallel and serial mediators linking smartphone addiction to sleep quality in Chinese adolescents. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 612 adolescents (Mage = 14.2 years, SD = 1.6; 51.3% female) from four secondary schools in Hubei Province, China. Participants completed the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version, the Physical Activity Questionnaire for Adolescents, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and the Depression subscale of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21. Path analysis of observed composite scores with robust maximum likelihood estimation and bias-corrected bootstrapping (5,000 resamples) was used to test the proposed parallel and serial mediation model. Smartphone addiction was positively associated with poor sleep quality (β = .38, p <.001). Both physical activity (indirect effect = .04, 95% CI [.01,.07]) and depressive symptoms (indirect effect = .14, 95% CI [.09,.19]) significantly mediated this association in parallel. In addition, the serial pathway from smartphone addiction to low physical activity, elevated depressive symptoms, and poor sleep quality was significant (indirect effect = .02, 95% CI [.01,.04]). The mediators collectively accounted for 52.6% of the total effect. These findings suggest that problematic smartphone use is associated with poorer adolescent sleep through behavioral and psychological pathways involving reduced physical activity and elevated depressive symptoms. School-based interventions that promote physical activity while reducing problematic smartphone use may help protect adolescent sleep and mental health. Longitudinal and experimental designs are needed to establish causal direction and inform intervention development.

papers.title: Night-to-night sleep variability and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective cohort study with a complementary in vitro circadian-disruption experiment.
papers.abstract: Irregular sleep-wake patterns may disrupt circadian rhythms, but the dose-response relationship between night-to-night sleep variability and mortality and the association of sleep onset variability with death remain unclear. Using 4-7 valid days of wrist accelerometer data, including ≥1 weekend day, from 7,604 adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011-2014, linked to mortality through December 2019, we examined the within-person SDs of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time across nights and the sleep regularity index (SRI) in relation to all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. Survey-weighted Cox models were fitted across 20 imputed datasets and combined using Rubin's rules. Restricted cubic splines examined dose-response relationships. Complementary categorical, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) experiments repeated in three independent runs compared cellular responses under a regular dexamethasone schedule and four prespecified irregular schedule variants. Over a median follow-up of 81 months, 714 all-cause and 229 CVD deaths occurred. Each 1-hour increase in the across-night SD of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time was associated with all-cause mortality HRs of 1.22 (95% CI, 1.12-1.33), 1.19 (1.11-1.29), and 1.17 (1.05-1.31), respectively. The corresponding CVD mortality HRs were 1.21 (1.09-1.35), 1.22 (1.05-1.42), and 1.16 (0.94-1.42), respectively. Each 10-point lower SRI was associated with all-cause mortality (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.21-1.38) and CVD mortality (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.45). Across three independent HUVEC runs, the mean response across the four prespecified irregular schedule variants showed lower core clock-gene expression, lower Griess assay absorbance, and higher inflammatory and adhesion-marker expression than the regular schedule. Greater night-to-night sleep irregularity was associated with higher hazards of all-cause and CVD mortality, although these associations were modest compared with those of older age, hypertension, and diabetes in the same models. The complementary cellular experiment showed differences between the regular dexamethasone schedule and the prespecified irregular schedule set.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.abstract: AI-driven generative art is changing the scope of artistic creation, but the principles behind its aesthetics and the perception of its outcomes remain relatively unexplored, especially concerning culturally specific art forms. The present study investigates how viewers cognitively, affectively, and evaluatively process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. We introduce the concept of expressive expansion as a viewer-perceived psychological effect - the tendency for AI-generated ink works to elicit higher ratings of expressiveness and dynamic tension than traditional counterparts - and examine its neural and behavioral correlates using a multimodal paradigm. Stimuli generated using a pre-trained Stable Diffusion architecture were assessed according to three aesthetic metrics along with traditional and digital non-AI artworks by 120 respondents equally split into professional artists and non-artists. Multidimensional measurement based on eye-tracking, semantic differential rating, and EEG showed that, under blind viewing conditions, AI-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-AI works, suggesting that they engaged broader attentional exploration and increased attentional engagement as indexed by implicit behavioral and neural measures. Professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness evaluation scores but differed considerably in their cultural authenticity perception, suggesting a dissociation between aesthetic appeal and cultural validity. These findings are consistent with a dual-pathway interpretive framework in which perceptual-affective and cultural-evaluative responses can dissociate as a function of artistic expertise - an account advanced as consistent with the observed dissociation rather than as a mechanism established by the present data - and contribute to the emerging empirical literature on audience responses to AI-generated art in culturally specific domains. All conclusions are restricted to the selected stimulus sets under the present experimental conditions. The source code, LoRA model weights, and experimental datasets will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/15100376058/ink-painting-ai-expressive-expansion (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20540420).

papers.title: Not all stress is equal: Examination stress and cortisol reactivity are associated with exploratory species-level variation but not broad restructuring of the gut microbiome.
papers.abstract: Psychological stress has been implicated in gut microbiome variation, but human evidence remains inconsistent and often does not distinguish exposure to stressful contexts from individual differences in physiological stress reactivity. This repeated-measures study examined whether naturalistic examination stress and post-awakening cortisol reactivity were associated with gut microbiome diversity, community composition, and species-level differential abundance. Thirty-nine healthy university students were assessed during examination and non-examination periods. At each assessment, participants completed validated measures of perceived stress, anxiety, affect, self-esteem, sleep, diet, and physical activity; provided salivary cortisol samples at awakening, 30 min, and 45 min post-awakening; and collected a stool sample for whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing. Post-awakening cortisol reactivity was indexed using area under the curve with respect to increase. Examination stress was associated with increased perceived stress, state and trait anxiety, negative affect, poorer subjective sleep, and amplified post-awakening cortisol reactivity. Alpha and beta diversity of the gut microbiome did not differ between examination and non-examination periods, and within-subject changes in community composition were not associated with changes in cortisol reactivity. However, exploratory species-level analyses identified nominal selective microbial differences. Examination stress was associated with higher relative abundance of Dialister massiliensis and Lawsonibacter asaccharolyticus, alongside lower Duodenibacillus massiliensis and Sutterella wadsworthensis. Cortisol reactivity showed distinct associations with higher Roseburia hominis and Ruminococcus bicirculans, and lower Methanobrevibacter smithii. Within-subject increases in cortisol reactivity also covaried with higher Dabirmavirus hominis, Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens and lower Coprococcus catus. Short-term examination stress was associated with marked psychological and endocrine responses but was not accompanied by broad restructuring of the adult gut microbiome. Instead, exploratory findings suggest that examination stress and cortisol reactivity may be reflected in selective species-level microbial variation, supporting further longitudinal and functional investigation of stress-related microbiome dynamics.

papers.title: Multidimensional factors associated with childhood obesity severity in southern China: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Childhood obesity poses a major public health challenge, yet evidence on its graded associations with modifiable factors across dietary, behavioral, familial, and socioeconomic dimensions remains limited, particularly in Southeast China. This study aimed to comprehensively examine the multidimensional factors associated with childhood obesity. This cross-sectional study included 680 school-aged children from Fujian Province, China. Data on perinatal factors, family weight status, parental education, dietary intake, physical activity, and sleep behaviors were collected. Obesity severity was classified into four ordinal groups based on Chinese national standards. Ordinal logistic regression models were used to estimate associations. Group differences for categorical variables were assessed using the chi-square test. Birth weight and infant feeding mode showed no significant association with obesity severity. Maternal care was associated with lower obesity risk in girls. Significant familial clustering was observed for paternal obesity (OR = 1.93, 95% CI: 1.20-3.06) and sibling obesity (OR = 2.26, 95% CI: 1.16-4.29). Lower parental education correlated with greater obesity severity. Breakfast frequency declined progressively with increasing obesity severity. At lunch and dinner, intakes of poultry, seafood, vegetables, fruits, and legumes decreased significantly across groups. Poultry intake at lunch was significantly associated with lower obesity risk (OR = 0.558, 95% CI: 0.354-0.878). Barbecue, cold drinks, and puffed foods were associated with increased obesity risk (OR = 1.763, 95% CI: 1.096-2.836). In contrast, nuts (OR = 0.477, 95% CI: 0.282-0.807) and biscuits (OR = 0.483, 95% CI: 0.322-0.723) showed significant were associated with lower risk. Regarding physical activity, ball sports (OR = 0.457, 95% CI: 0.227-0.918) and walking (OR = 0.368, 95% CI: 0.180-0.751) were significantly associated with lower obesity risk. Later bedtime and shorter sleep duration exhibited associations with obesity severity. Childhood obesity severity is associated with multiple factors, including familial weight status, parental education, meal diversity, snacking patterns, physical activity, and sleep behaviors. These findings may inform multifaceted, family centered approaches that could be considered for the prevention of childhood obesity.

papers.title: Optimized hybrid Transformer-based model for EEG classification: application to wheelchair control.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to improve the classification of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs), thus enabling more reliable user interactions in assistive technologies such as autonomous wheelchairs. The study contributes by systematically investigating and comparing the performance of both simple (Transformer, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)) and hybrid deep learning architectures (Transformer + CNN, Transformer + LSTM, CNN + LSTM) for EEG signal classification using multiple evaluation metrics, including accuracy, ROC AUC, confusion matrices, and prediction time. The findings demonstrate that the Transformer + CNN hybrid model consistently outperforms all other architectures, thereby achieving perfect classification accuracy (1.00), zero misclassifications, flawless AUC scores (1.000), and a competitive inference time (1.17 s), thus making it highly suitable for real-time MI-BCI applications. In contrast, simple models, particularly LSTM, show lower accuracies and reduced stabilities. Overall, this study highlights the advantage of combining attention mechanisms and convolutional architectures to effectively capture both spatial and contextual patterns in nonstationary EEG signals, thus establishing Transformer-based hybrid models as a promising approach for robust, real-time EEG classifications in next-generation MI-BCI systems.

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that significantly impacts the cognitive functions and behaviour of individuals. It is characterized by abnormal brain lateralization in key brain regions linked to attention and cognitive control. This study aimed to explore and analyze the brainwave patterns linked to left and right brain dominance in ADHD, ADHD subtype, and control group using electroencephalography (EEG) spectral features, which have not been investigated in prior studies. Our study examined variations in alpha, beta, theta, and other frequency bands between the brain's left and right hemispheres, employing methodologies like EEG recordings with topographical views and statistical tests. The Asymmetric Index findings suggest a differential power spectrum density (PSD) pattern in ADHD subjects, with a higher average PSD in the right brain (RB) during working states and in the left brain (LB) during resting states. In addition, our corroborative study also uncovered that in ADHD subjects, theta and alpha waves are more dominant in the left hemispheric region, irrespective of the task state, and theta waves are notably prominent in the frontal region. The results of our novel study, supported by statistical analyses and topographical views, not only enhance our understanding of ADHD but also open avenues for more targeted and effective approaches in diagnosing and understanding the neurobiological underpinnings of ADHD and its subtypes.

papers.title: Cannabinoids in oncology: pharmacology, clinical applications, and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Cannabis and cannabinoid products are increasingly used by patients with cancer for symptom management and supportive care. Although cannabis is widely used to alleviate cancer- and treatment-related symptoms, many patients also believe that it possesses direct anticancer activity. This review provides a comprehensive pharmacologic and clinical assessment of cannabinoids in oncology, integrating the endocannabinoid system, cannabinoid receptor signaling, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic applications, adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, and emerging antitumor research. The strongest clinical evidence supports selected cannabinoid preparations for refractory chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, whereas evidence for cancer-related pain, appetite stimulation, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and opioid-sparing effects remains limited or inconsistent. Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) differ substantially in receptor pharmacology, psychoactive effects, metabolism, and toxicity, with important implications for product selection, dosing, and interactions with anticancer and supportive-care medications. Preclinical studies demonstrate antiproliferative, proapoptotic, antiangiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects across multiple tumor models; however, cannabinoid signaling is highly context dependent and may also promote tumor progression in selected settings. Human evidence for direct anticancer activity remains sparse, consisting predominantly of small early-phase studies and observational data, with no established improvement in tumor response, progression-free survival, or overall survival. Particular caution is warranted regarding neuropsychiatric and cardiovascular toxicity, pharmacokinetic drug interactions, and the potential influence of cannabis on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Overall, cannabinoids have defined but limited roles in supportive oncology, while their direct antitumor potential remains investigational. Future studies should prioritize standardized formulations, pharmacologically informed dosing, rigorous randomized designs, clinically meaningful endpoints, and biomarker-based approaches to define therapeutic benefit and risk.

papers.title: Multimodal digital assessment of early recovery after chest tube omission in early-stage lung cancer patients undergoing wedge resection: a post hoc analysis of a prospective cohort.
papers.abstract: Given the limited surgical trauma associated with wedge resection, the clinical impact of routine chest tube drainage may be more apparent in early postoperative recovery than in safety outcomes alone. We used a multimodal digital platform integrating wearable monitoring and electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) to compare recovery after wedge resection with and without chest tube placement. This study was a post hoc secondary analysis of prospectively collected data from a registered single-center observational cohort (NCT06118229). We included 98 patients from the parent cohort who had M0 primary lung cancer, underwent wedge resection, and had evaluable perioperative clinical and digital data; 54 were managed without chest tube placement and 44 with routine drainage. Propensity score matching yielded 34 matched pairs. Compared with the chest tube group, the no chest tube group had a shorter postoperative hospital stay (2.51±1.11 vs. 3.14±1.03 days; P=0.02). Differences were most apparent in patient-reported recovery on postoperative day 2, with lower pain scores (2.79±2.11 vs. 4.08±2.07; P=0.03), less restless sleep (1.98±1.86 vs. 3.49±2.32; P=0.01), and less drowsiness (2.07±1.35 vs. 3.08±1.70; P=0.02). Wearable-derived physiologic trajectories were largely similar, although oxygen saturation on postoperative day 1 was higher in the no chest tube group (97.22%±1.64% vs. 96.05%±1.56%; P=0.003). After wedge resection, omission of routine chest tube drainage was associated with a more favorable early patient-reported recovery, whereas physiologic differences were modest. Multimodal digital assessment may offer a practical and patient-centered approach to postoperative monitoring after minimally invasive thoracic surgery.

papers.title: Multimodal art intervention for flourishing in lonely university students: psychological and exploratory neurophysiological outcomes.
papers.abstract: Loneliness is highly prevalent among university students and is associated with reduced positive functioning. However, evidence concerning multimodal art interventions for flourishing-related outcomes in this population remains limited. This study examined whether an eight-week, group-based multimodal art intervention could improve psychological flourishing, state positive affect, aesthetic experience, and exploratory wearable electroencephalography (EEG) indices among lonely university students. Sixty students with elevated loneliness (20-item UCLA Loneliness Scale score ≥ 44) and below-flourishing mental health, as assessed using the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form, were randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n = 30) or a wait-list control group (n = 30). The intervention comprised eight weekly group sessions integrating guided music listening, visual creation, movement or role-play, and group sharing. Outcomes were assessed over time and analyzed for Group × Time interactions. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for flourishing, F(2, 112) = 4.57, p = 0.012, partial η 2 = 0.075; positive affect F(2, 112) = 19.45, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.258; aesthetic experience F(2, 112) = 24.37, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.303; and the relaxation index F(2, 112) = 3.30, p = 0.040, partial η 2 = 0.056. The Group × Time interaction for the attention index was not significant. The findings provide preliminary evidence that a group-based multimodal art intervention may enhance aesthetic engagement, positive affect, psychological flourishing, and alpha-based relaxation among lonely university students, although attention-related EEG indices remained unchanged. Multimodal art programs may offer a feasible and accessible approach to supporting university students' well-being.

papers.title: An innovative hybrid cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia approach to insomnia treatment: a retrospective chart review study.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a common and significant concern within family medicine; however, there is limited access to qualified sleep specialists trained in the first-line treatment: cognitive behavioral treatment for insomnia (CBT-I). Technology advancements allowed for "app delivery" of CBT-I, but platforms do not customize treatment. To our knowledge, DrLullaby was the first to offer a hybrid approach, to improve behavioral sleep medicine access, through "tech-enabled services," including telehealth sessions alongside our sleep data portal. We hypothesized that this approach would yield improved sleep outcomes. A retrospective chart review of patients who engaged in hybrid CBT-I treatment (n = 155) was performed. The sample was split into two groups based on treatment protocol: (G1) hybrid CBT-I, non-sleep medication tapering (n = 113) and (G2) sleep medication tapering (n = 42). CBT-I-trained clinicians provided virtual insomnia treatment and assigned lessons in the sleep data portal for support between sessions. Self-reported sleep log and medication tapering (for G2) data were analyzed pre-and-post treatment using one-way repeated-measures ANOVA. Sleep metrics significantly improved from baseline to posttreatment for the hybrid CBT-I group, including total sleep time, sleep onset latency, wake after sleep onset, and sleep efficiency (Ps < 0.001). Almost 67% of patients in the sleep medication tapering group completely discontinued their sleep medication(s). DrLullaby's hybrid approach resulted in a significant reduction of insomnia symptoms and sleep medication dosage. Virtual delivery of tech-enabled CBT-I, alongside sleep medication tapering, may be a viable referral option for family medicine clinicians who otherwise lack access to the first-line insomnia treatment.

papers.title: Exploring a Range of Potential Factors Promoting and Constraining EF in South African Preschoolers.
papers.abstract: Socioeconomic disadvantage is widely associated with poorer cognitive and educational outcomes. However, emerging evidence suggests that children in low-income contexts may demonstrate resilience in executive function (EF) development. This study examined the predictors of EF in South African preschoolers from disadvantaged communities to identify modifiable, context-specific influences. 125 Children (aged 3-5 years) and their caregivers were recruited from 15 early childhood centers in Cape Town. Children completed three tablet-based EF tasks from the Early Years Toolbox measuring working memory, inhibition, shifting, while caregivers reported on demographic variables, household assets, child sleep, child screen time, child exposure to violence, and parenting practices. Multiple linear regressions examined predictors of child EF, with exploratory analyses on a subset (n = 22) for hair cortisol analysis. Older child age (β = 0.37, p < 0.001), caregiver secondary education (β = 0.22, p = 0.003), and fewer sleep difficulties (β = -0.45, p = 0.042) significantly predicted higher child EF scores, together explaining 25% of variance. Household assets, screen time, violence exposure, and parenting scores were non-significant. In the subsample, hair cortisol concentration correlated positively with EF (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.009), suggesting potential adaptive calibration under adversity. Findings highlight that modifiable proximal factors (e.g., caregiver education and child sleep) shape EF development more strongly than socioeconomic indicators. Results challenge the presumed universality of SES-EF gradients and underscore the importance of culturally grounded, contextually validated measures for understanding resilience and early cognitive development in Majority World settings.

papers.title: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study of Chronic Urticaria in Chinese Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, and Effect on Disease Management.
papers.abstract: To investigate the epidemiology and risk factors for chronic urticaria (CU) in Chinese adults with cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), and its effect on CMD recognition and management. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional analysis using data from the 2018-2019 China Chronic Disease and Risk Factor Surveillance, which included 118,036 adults with CMDs. Weighted CU prevalence and CMD awareness, treatment, and control rates (stratified by CU status) were estimated using a complex survey design, whereas risk factors for CU were identified using multivariable logistic regression. The weighted CU prevalence among patients with CMDs was 2.90%, peaking at 3.94% in 60-69-year-old individuals, and was higher in females (3.41%) than in males (2.56%), especially in rural areas. Key risk factors included current smoking (odds ratio [ OR] 1.17, 95% confidence interval [ CI]: 1.06-1.29) and abnormal sleep duration (< 5 h: OR 1.79, 95% CI: 1.61-1.99; > 10 h: OR 1.39, 95% CI: 1.19-1.61). Patients with CU showed stronger association with improved CMD awareness (hypertension: 50.71% vs. 40.27%; diabetes: 47.14% vs. 36.21%; dyslipidemia: 30.71% vs. 17.12%) and treatment rates (hypertension: 41.37% vs. 34.22%; diabetes: 41.31% vs. 32.52%; dyslipidemia: 18.29% vs. 9.94%) than non-CU patients but with comparable control rates. CU is prevalent in patients with CMD and associated with distinct demographic and lifestyle risk factors. Although CU facilitates earlier detection of CMD, it does not improve disease control, indicating the need for integrated dermatology-cardiometabolic care.

papers.title: Acupuncture for older adults with dementia in residential care homes: an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Dementia harms the mental health of older adults and poses a significant caregiver burden. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture in managing cognitive decline and related symptoms in older adults with dementia. Eligible participants were recruited from 19 local residential care homes for older people in Hong Kong, China, from 5 October 2021 to 27 August 2024, in an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial. 118 participants were randomised to acupuncture and care-as-usual control (n=59 in each group) for 12 weeks. The analyses were on the intention-to-treat population. The primary outcome was the mean baseline-to-endpoint change of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included the functional independence, pain, depressive and sleep symptoms. 85.6% (101/118) of participants completed the study. The primary outcome, MoCA, was not significantly improved in week 12. Subgroup analyses showed that the treatment effect on MoCA appeared to differ across dementia severity strata. Acupuncture was superior over control in improving functional independence (the Chinese version of the Modified Barthel Index, mean difference=4.12, 95% confidence interval=0.81, 7.44, P=0.015; standardised effect size=0.29). All treatment-related adverse events were mild, and 2 nontreatment-related death cases were reported. While no significant effect in cognitive function was observed, acupuncture was associated with an improvement in functional independence, and the treatment effect on cognition might differ across dementia severity strata. This warrants further validation of the exploratory results, identifying a subpopulation of older adults with dementia who could gain more benefits from acupuncture in improving cognitive function. www.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04305951, date of registration: 10/03/2020.

papers.title: Neurological Assessment Tools and Inflammatory Biomarkers for Predicting Cerebral Palsy in Neonatal HIE.
papers.abstract: To evaluate temporal changes in serum interleukin-40 (IL-40), hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), and procalcitonin (PCT) levels between early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) undergoing therapeutic hypothermia (TH), and to determine the prognostic value of these biomarkers together with the Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination (HNNE), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting cerebral palsy (CP). Thirty-five neonates with HIE treated with TH and 20 healthy term neonates were prospectively enrolled. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels were measured before and after TH. Associations between biomarkers, HNNE, aEEG, MRI findings, and CP at follow-up were evaluated. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels decreased significantly between the early and post-rewarming measurements (all p < 0.001). Although biomarker levels differed from controls, they were not associated with subsequent CP. In contrast, HNNE, aEEG, and MRI showed strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP among surviving infants. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels showed significant temporal decreases between the early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with HIE undergoing TH; however, these biomarkers did not predict subsequent CP among surviving infants. HNNE, aEEG, and MRI each demonstrated strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP when evaluated individually in this cohort.
papers.journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

papers.title: Prolonged Breastfeeding at 18 Months and Early Childhood Caries at Age 3 Years: A Population-Based Cohort Study From Japan.
papers.abstract: Breastfeeding is recommended to 2 years or beyond, but its association with early childhood caries (ECC) after infancy remains uncertain, partly because of inconsistent adjustment for confounders and reverse causation. To examine whether breastfeeding at 18 months was associated with dental caries at age 3 years. Japanese check-up cohort (2014-2019). Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs), adjusting for sex, regular sweetened juice consumption, screen time > 1 h/day, parental tooth-brushing assistance, single-parent household and parental employment; sensitivity analyses adjusted for or excluded those with 18-month caries. Of 69 165 children, 12 788 (18.5%) were breastfeeding at 18 months. Any caries (35.9% vs. 23.7%) and severe caries (19.2% vs. 10.5%) were more common in breastfeeding children. After behavioural and socioeconomic adjustment, breastfeeding remained associated with any caries (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.82-1.98) and severe caries (OR 2.14, 95% CI 2.03-2.26); associations persisted after adjustment for caries at 18 months (any caries OR 1.74; severe caries OR 1.87). Breastfeeding at 18 months was independently associated with higher odds of ECC at 3 years; reverse causation alone did not account for this. Findings support integrating targeted oral-health counselling, including avoidance of feed-to-sleep and post-feed oral cleaning, into breastfeeding support after infancy.

papers.title: Inhibition of Cerebellar Dentate Nucleus-Zona Incerta Glutamatergic Circuit Improves Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model.
papers.abstract: Patients with chronic temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) frequently experience various sleep disorders, characterized by reduced sleep duration, diminished sleep stages, and disrupted sleep patterns. Recent research has identified a population of GABAergic neurons in the ventral zona incerta (ZI) that is instrumental in promoting sleep, along with a neural pathway that connects the cerebellar dentate nucleus (CDN) to the ZI. However, the precise role of this circuit in regulating sleep patterns remains inadequately understood. This study employed anatomical, chemogenetic, optogenetic, and immunofluorescence staining techniques to investigate the potential of the CDN-ZI circuit in ameliorating sleep disturbances associated with TLE. Our findings indicate that pilocarpine-treated mice exhibit significant sleep fragmentation and reduced sleep duration, particularly during non-rapid eye movement sleep. By employing optogenetic and chemogenetic methods to target CDN glutamatergic neurons, we observed a decrease in sleep fragmentation, an increase in overall sleep duration, and an enhancement in sleep quality in pilocarpine-treated mice. The inhibition of the CDN-ZI glutamatergic circuit through optogenetic and chemogenetic methods resulted in substantial improvements in sleep disturbances following TLE. Targeting the CDN-ZI glutamatergic circuit represents a promising therapeutic strategy for addressing sleep disorders resulting from chronic TLE.

papers.title: Three PRR proteins interact with ARF10 and ARF16 to enhance ABI5 activation and auxin-stimulated ABA responses during Arabidopsis seed germination.
papers.abstract: The circadian clock and auxin regulate abscisic acid (ABA)-induced delayed seed germination in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the crosstalk between circadian clock and auxin in modulating ABA signaling remain obscure. Here, we found that the central circadian clock proteins PSEUDO-RESPONSE REGULATOR5 (PRR5), PRR7, and PRR9 are crucial for auxin-increased ABA responses. Disrupting PRR5, PRR7, and PRR9 simultaneously conferred germinating seeds substantially less sensitive to combined auxin and ABA treatment, whereas PRR5 overexpression partially restores the ABA-hyposensitive phenotype of the auxin signaling-defective mutants (i.e., axr3-1). PRR5, PRR7, and PRR9 interact with the auxin-dependent transcription factors AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR10 (ARF10) and ARF16. Consistently, PRR5, PRR7, and PRR9 cooperate with ARF10/ARF16 to promote auxin-enhanced ABA responses. Importantly, PRR5 and ARF16 synergistically stimulate the transcriptional activation by ABSCISIC ACID INSENSITIVE5 (ABI5, a master activator of ABA signaling) and the enrichment of ABI5 at the promoters of downstream targets. Moreover, PRR5 and ARF16 coordinately enhance the ABA-induced accumulation of ABI5 in germinating seeds. Collectively, our results demonstrate that the auxin stimulation on ABA signaling requires PRR5, PRR7, and PRR9, and explain the mechanism by which PRR proteins synergize with ARF10/ARF16 to activate ABI5 and integrate the circadian clock, auxin, and ABA pathways.
